title: Postmortem of database outage of January 31
technical_topics: PostgreSQL; replication; WAL; backup and restore; operator error
failure_mechanism_summary: Database load caused replication lag; missing WAL archiving forced manual resynchronization, during which an operator deleted the primary data directory, extending the outage and causing data loss.
selection_evidence: The report states that WAL segments needed by the secondary had already been removed and presents separate 5 Whys analyses for the outage and the long restoration.
uncertainties_limitations: The narrative combines several contributing failures and human actions; editorial review must avoid reducing it to a single operator mistake.
recommendation_rationale: Exceptional primary-source treatment of database failure, recovery readiness, observability, backups, and human factors.

title: CircleCI Status - Jobs not starting
technical_topics: Kubernetes; kube-proxy; kubelet; iptables; service networking; RabbitMQ
failure_mechanism_summary: A staged Kubernetes upgrade left kubelet and kube-proxy at incompatible versions; repeated iptables restore failures corrupted node networking and broke service-to-service communication.
selection_evidence: The text reports a version mismatch causing widespread networking failures and includes the concrete error: Failed to execute iptables-restore.
uncertainties_limitations: The same report includes two follow-on RabbitMQ incidents, so the primary Kubernetes failure and secondary queue failures must remain distinguishable.
recommendation_rationale: Strong Kubernetes networking case with concrete symptoms, commands, recovery steps, and follow-on effects.

title: Summary of the Amazon DynamoDB Service Disruption and Related Impacts in the US-East Region
technical_topics: DynamoDB; metadata service; distributed storage; timeouts; retry storm; cascading failure
failure_mechanism_summary: Slow metadata responses caused storage servers to time out, disqualify themselves, and retry; the added retries prevented metadata load from falling and amplified the regional disruption.
selection_evidence: The report says servers that could not retrieve membership data within the allowed time retried and temporarily removed themselves from serving requests.
uncertainties_limitations: AWS terminology and the number of dependent-service effects make the account dense; causal ordering should be checked during review.
recommendation_rationale: High-value distributed-systems example of feedback loops, retry amplification, dependency cascades, and corrective actions.

title: Incident details | Google Cloud Service Health
technical_topics: API control plane; policy replication; null pointer; crash loop; Spanner; thundering herd
failure_mechanism_summary: A globally replicated policy with blank fields exercised an unprotected code path, triggered a null pointer crash loop in Service Control, and produced a thundering-herd recovery load on Spanner.
selection_evidence: The report explicitly states that blank policy fields hit a null pointer, crashed regional binaries, and that restarting tasks created a herd effect on underlying infrastructure.
uncertainties_limitations: This is a provider status report; product-specific terminology needs contextualization before later chunking.
recommendation_rationale: Excellent control-plane incident combining unsafe rollout, missing error handling, global replication, and recovery amplification.

title: Details of the Cloudflare outage on July 2 2019
technical_topics: WAF; regular expressions; catastrophic backtracking; CPU exhaustion; global deployment
failure_mechanism_summary: A globally deployed WAF rule contained a pathological regular expression whose backtracking exhausted proxy CPU across the network; removed safeguards and rapid deployment increased blast radius.
selection_evidence: The article says the expression backtracked enormously, exhausted HTTP/HTTPS-serving CPU, and drove network-wide CPU close to 100 percent.
uncertainties_limitations: The login/block heuristic appears inconsistent with the substantial article text and requires manual confirmation; the report emphasizes multiple vulnerabilities rather than one root cause.
recommendation_rationale: Canonical primary-source example of unsafe global rollout, performance pathology, missing guardrails, and layered contributing factors.

title: Post-Incident Review on the Atlassian April 2022 outage
technical_topics: maintenance automation; tenant deletion; backup restoration; incident communication; long recovery
failure_mechanism_summary: A maintenance script deleted customer sites instead of removing a deprecated application, forcing a complex multi-day restoration process for 775 customers.
selection_evidence: The report identifies the maintenance script as the source of the outage and documents restoration and customer communication across April 5 through April 18.
uncertainties_limitations: Very long document; the login/block alert needs manual adjudication, and later chunking must preserve the distinction between deletion, restoration, and communications.
recommendation_rationale: Rare and detailed primary-source account of destructive automation, tenant recovery, operational readiness, and prolonged incident management.

title: A Byzantine failure in the real world
technical_topics: network switch; partial failure; Byzantine fault; Raft; leader election; control plane
failure_mechanism_summary: A partially failed switch gave cluster nodes conflicting connectivity views, causing repeated tied Raft elections and leaving the control-plane datastore read-only.
selection_evidence: The article explicitly describes cluster members having conflicting views of reality and explains how node votes repeatedly tied without a reachable leader.
uncertainties_limitations: The heuristic does not mark root cause despite a strong mechanism narrative; hardware behavior and distributed-consensus effects must both be retained.
recommendation_rationale: Distinctive distributed-systems case showing why partial network failures can be more dangerous than clean failures.

title: Postmortem for July 27 outage of the Manta service | Joyent
technical_topics: PostgreSQL; transaction wraparound; autovacuum; locking; metadata tier
failure_mechanism_summary: PostgreSQL anti-wraparound autovacuum and an application query that requested an unnecessarily broad lock combined to block Manta metadata operations.
selection_evidence: The report observes autovacuum running to prevent wraparound while other queries blocked and provides a dedicated Summary of Root Cause.
uncertainties_limitations: The authors initially did not understand why autovacuum blocked queries; preserve that investigative uncertainty and the interaction between database and application behavior.
recommendation_rationale: Strong database-locking case with timeline, evidence, evolving hypotheses, mitigation, and prevention.

title: Billing Incident Post-Mortem: Breakdown Analysis and Root Cause | Twilio
technical_topics: Redis; network partition; replication; read-only mode; retries; billing idempotency
failure_mechanism_summary: A Redis disruption and faulty restart configuration left the billing master read-only; recharge retries charged cards before balances could be updated, producing repeated charges.
selection_evidence: The account states that redis-master booted as a slave of itself in read-only mode and that billing transactions then triggered recharge attempts against zero balances.
uncertainties_limitations: The source URL redirects through Twilio's current blog structure; review should verify that historical details remain complete.
recommendation_rationale: Compact but technically rich example of partition recovery, unsafe state, retry behavior, and missing transactional idempotency.

title: DNS Outage Post Mortem - The GitHub Blog
technical_topics: DNS; Puppet; configuration management; circular dependency; memory exhaustion
failure_mechanism_summary: A Puppet manifest restarted only the authoritative DNS process after an IP change; incident-response automation then rebuilt zones through an internal API that depended on DNS, deepening the outage.
selection_evidence: The report states that the caching nameserver queried an IP no longer serving DNS because only the authoritative server had restarted, beginning a cascade of events.
uncertainties_limitations: The root_cause completeness flag is false even though causal details are explicit; review should preserve the multiple stages rather than force one label.
recommendation_rationale: Excellent configuration and recovery-automation case illustrating hidden circular dependencies during incident response.

title: Summary of the Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Service Event in Northern Virginia US-EAST-1 Region
technical_topics: Kinesis; shard placement; status messages; host failure detection; redistribution storm; dependency cascade
failure_mechanism_summary: Uneven placement put many low-throughput shards on a few hosts; oversized status messages were mistaken for host failures, triggering redistribution and overloading secure-connection provisioning.
selection_evidence: The report identifies one impaired Kinesis cell and explains how the new architecture's shard distribution and management behavior propagated impact to dependent AWS services.
uncertainties_limitations: Many downstream services are discussed; editorial review should keep the initiating cell failure separate from secondary effects.
recommendation_rationale: Valuable capacity-management and queueing case involving skew, false failure detection, redistribution storms, and platform dependencies.

title: Slack's Outage on January 4th 2021
technical_topics: AWS networking; packet loss; web tier; autoscaling; provisioning; recovery
failure_mechanism_summary: Underlying network problems caused packet loss and backend latency, saturating web workers; attempts to add 1200 servers exposed provisioning bottlenecks and complicated recovery.
selection_evidence: The report says packet loss increased backend-call latency and saturated web-tier resources, while the attempted 1200-server scale-up did not work as intended.
uncertainties_limitations: The heuristic does not mark root cause and the provider-side initiating event is described at limited depth; treat it as a documented mechanism and recovery account, not a complete AWS RCA.
recommendation_rationale: Strong example of misleading utilization signals, autoscaling under network degradation, and recovery capacity constraints.

title: Summary of Windows Azure Service Disruption on Feb 29th 2012 | Microsoft Azure Blog
technical_topics: certificates; leap year; date arithmetic; Fabric Controller; global outage
failure_mechanism_summary: Incorrect date arithmetic generated certificates ending on the nonexistent February 29 2013; certificate rejection disrupted Fabric Controller operations and cloud-service management.
selection_evidence: The primary source presents a root-cause analysis of the February 29 disruption and explains Fabric Controllers, agents, certificates, recovery, and prevention.
uncertainties_limitations: Older Azure architecture and terminology reduce direct modern applicability, but the validation and calendrical edge-case lessons remain relevant.
recommendation_rationale: High-quality configuration and validation failure with explicit causality, timeline, platform context, and corrective measures.

title: Tarsnap outage 2016-07-24 10:15:19--11:40:04
technical_topics: filesystem capacity; unbounded logging; S3 retries; batch processing; monitoring
failure_mechanism_summary: A background S3 cleanup process retried persistent failures and logged without bounds until the filesystem filled, causing service writes and the server process to fail.
selection_evidence: The report says the outage culminated in a full filesystem and describes finding and deleting the runaway log before restarting the service.
uncertainties_limitations: The precipitating change in Amazon S3 behavior remained undiagnosed, and the summary_context heuristic is false; preserve that uncertainty.
recommendation_rationale: Concise primary account of a classic unbounded-resource and observability failure with clear operational lessons.

title: crates.io Postmortem: Broken Crate Downloads
technical_topics: deployment; URL generation; object storage; monitoring; rollback; retry amplification
failure_mechanism_summary: A deployment introduced a download-URL generation bug that broke all crates.io downloads; Cargo retries amplified traffic until the deployment was rolled back.
selection_evidence: The report records 4.71K requests per second and about 3.7 million failed requests, including retries, during the 13-minute incident.
uncertainties_limitations: Short incident and rapid rollback provide less recovery complexity than higher-priority candidates, but evidence and preventive actions are explicit.
recommendation_rationale: Clean deploy-regression case with measurable impact, fast detection, rollback, retry amplification, and concrete follow-up work.
